### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **56** of **208** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **148** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9dacccf96127755bd196e1844ce5c4cd61717d57` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9c798fdb390a53e27033d0b9f186480df4c539d7` — the merge of head `c8e5fee888af2f7cad5ed0b42cc4813784e0027e` into base `9dacccf96127755bd196e1844ce5c4cd61717d57`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 9c798fdb390a53e27033d0b9f186480df4c539d7 && git checkout 9c798fdb390a53e27033d0b9f186480df4c539d7

git fetch origin 9dacccf96127755bd196e1844ce5c4cd61717d57 c8e5fee888af2f7cad5ed0b42cc4813784e0027e && git checkout -B drift-repro 9dacccf96127755bd196e1844ce5c4cd61717d57 && git merge --no-ff c8e5fee888af2f7cad5ed0b42cc4813784e0027e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9dacccf96127755bd196e1844ce5c4cd61717d57
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c8e5fee888af2f7cad5ed0b42cc4813784e0027e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts + packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.object-validations.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-validation-locale-negotiation.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-object-validation-message-i18n.test.ts, ui/packages/plugin-kanban/src/ObjectKanban.tsx, .changeset/27135-object-validation-message-i18n.md; the code those hunks make claims about, read on `origin/main` `9dacccf9`: packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts (`authoredRuleMessage`, `checkConditional`), packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts (`ValidationMessageContext`, `resolveFieldLabel`), packages/objectql/src/engine-validation-messages.ts (`validationMessageContext`, `negotiatedMessageLocale`), packages/services/service-i18n/src/file-i18n-adapter.ts (`t`, `resolveFromLocale`, `getTranslations`), packages/core/src/fallbacks/memory-i18n.ts (`t`), packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts (`translateMetaList`, `translateMetaDocument`, `translationBundleOf`, `metaTranslateOptions`, `metaRequestLocale`), packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-routes.ts (the locale-keyed ETag), packages/rest/src/meta-collection-routes.ts (`Vary`), packages/rest/src/form-routes.ts L300-325, packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts (`pushValidationMessages`), packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts (`_validations`), ui/packages/react/src/hooks/useSettledSchema.ts (the kanban's `objectDef` source), skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md L167, content/docs/ui/translations.mdx L388-396, docs/adr/0029 D9.2 and D9.2a; PR #27133 (body, file list, merge `ec66ac0d`); card #27135 body and comments 6463784251, 6465192030, 6466141109, 6466175269; PR #27202 body, file list, both commits, `compare/ac138e64e...c8e5fee88`, net diff against main, the one PR comment (docs-drift bot), and the head's check-runs.

_Card, PR, diff and cited code read 2026-10-28T11:04Z; the head was `c8e5fee88` at every read and had not moved._

### ① Derived judgments

**1. One key — holds.** `translateObjectValidations` (i18n-resolver.ts L3996-4038 at the head) spells the address with `objectValidationMessageKey(objectName, rule.name)` and walks it as a dotted path through each locale's data; rule-validator.ts L3769 `authoredRuleMessage` asks `II18nService.t` for the output of the same function. No second spelling and no second resolver: the locale ladder is the shared `localeChain` + `pickData` (`resolveBundleLocale`) every overlay in this file uses, and the write path negotiates the request tag with the same `resolveBundleLocale` over `getLocales()` (`negotiatedMessageLocale`) before an exact `t` lookup, so a bare `zh` reaches `zh-CN` on both. The spec test pins that the retired top-level `validationMessages` and a bare `objects.OBJECT.RULE.message` stay unread, and builds every bundle entry at the path `objectValidationMessageKey` spells, parsed by `TranslationBundleSchema`.

**2. `/meta` equals the refusal — holds, with three pre-existing edges shared with field labels.** The chains compared: the resolver walks `locale → fallbackChain = [getFallbackLocale()] → authored`, skipping the chain when `locale` is the `defaultLocale` (#15711); `FileI18nAdapter.t` walks `locale` exact → `fallbackLocale` → the key (miss) → the validator keeps the authored text. They agree on: a rule with no `name` (both authored: validator L3767, resolver L4015); a bundle with no entry (both authored); an inactive or warning-only rule (the overlay translates its `message` regardless of `active`/`severity`; no refusal is emitted for such a rule, so there is no second sentence to disagree with, and the kanban asks the gate before naming a rule); an extended object (both key on the merged object's `name`, and `pushValidationMessages` writes the same address for an `objectExtensions` rule, as i18n-standard.mdx documents); a tenant/org authored translation layer (`translationBundleOf` reads `getTranslations`, the merged static+authored view; `t` probes the same two maps authored-first — one precedence); a `conditional` rule (`checkConditional` hands the branch to `evaluateRule`, so the refusal carries the branch's own name and message; the overlay translates the branches and leaves the wrapper authored, pinned with a wrapper entry present in the bundle).
Where they can differ, none introduced here and each shared with field labels through the same `lookupObjectFieldAttr` / `resolveFieldLabel` pair: (a) a request for the default locale whose own bundle lacks the entry while the fallback locale's has it (the dev declared this); (b) an empty-string entry in the requested locale — `t` returns `''` and takes no fallback leg, so the validator keeps the authored text, while `localeChain` walks on and may serve the fallback locale's string; (c) `createMemoryI18n().t` reads the DEFAULT locale's bundle before `fallbackLocale` when the requested locale has no bundle at all. Recorded, not failed: the card's Expected is "the same way it overlays field labels", and that is what this is. The depth bound `MAX_VALIDATION_DEPTH = 10` equals the extractor's; the validator has none, so a branch nested deeper than ten is translated by the refusal and not by `/meta` — no extracted key exists for it either; negligible, noted.

**3. Nothing else moves — holds.** `label`/`pluralLabel`/`description`, `fields`, `actions` and `listViews` are computed before the new call and are untouched; the test pins `fields` and `actions` equal with and without `validations`, and no `validations` key added to a document without one. `/meta`'s shape is unchanged: the same array, each rule spread with only `message` replaced, and the authored array by reference when nothing matched. Caching: the item ETag is `simpleHash(locale + JSON.stringify(item))` (meta-item-read-routes.ts L649) and both transports send `Vary: Accept-Language` (meta-collection-routes.ts L219, L634) — unchanged by this PR, so no locale's translated message can be served from another locale's cached `/meta`. One door the PR body's reader measurement does not name: form-routes.ts L317 hands the public form's object schema to `translateMetadataDocument('object')`, so the anonymous form's served `validations[].message` is now translated too — the same direction as the refusal of the same submit, and the fix's intent; recorded. `formula-option-labels.ts` L150 and service-analytics L1168 pass `{ name, fields }` only — unaffected.

**4. The kanban comment — true at this head; `patch` honest.** `objectDef` is `useSettledSchema(schemaKey, dataSource)`, the adapter's `/api/v1/meta/object/:name` read, so ObjectKanban.tsx L1838-1840 now states what `/meta` serves: the bundle's `_validations.RULE.message` for the request locale, the refusal's string (edges in ①2 aside). `compare/ac138e64e...c8e5fee88` is one commit: the three comment lines and three changeset lines, nothing else. `@object-ui/plugin-kanban` is published (`18.2.0`, not in `.changeset/config.json` `ignore`), so the `patch` line is owed and is comment-only, as declared.

**5. Declarations — hold.** `Clause-②: no`: no Zod schema, no export, no `ObjectLike` member moved; no `api-surface/` or `authorable-surface/` shard is in the file list and `check:generated` had nothing to write. `Metadata-protocol: none`: no authorable key, value or meaning changes — the bundle key's meaning (the sentence a rejected write returns) is unchanged, it gains a second reader. `patch`: kind `none` on a behaviour fix. `Skills-docs: none`: skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md L167 ("`message` only — the sentence a rejected write returns") stays true; no `skills/**` or `.claude/skills/**` text teaches that `/meta` serves the message untranslated (grep `_validations`, `objectValidationMessageKey`, `untranslated`); the row now understates the key's reader set — a docs follow-up, not a false sentence. content/docs/ui/translations.mdx L388-396 likewise stays true. `Fixes #27135` is complete: the card's Expected (overlay from the one key; authored on a miss) and its "is a server-side test owed?" question are both answered.

**6. Tests — pin the claims; nothing weakened.** Spec (12): the overlay in `zh-CN`; `zh` → `zh-CN`; the declared chain then authored; the `translateMetadataDocument('object')` door; no input mutation; nameless rule, missing entry, empty entry, no bundle; no other spelling read; `fields`/`actions` unchanged; no key added. ObjectQL (+1): `translateObject(..., { locale, fallbackChain: ['en'] })` as `/meta` calls it, against the real engine's refusal (`ql.update` → `authoredRuleMessage`) for `zh-CN`, `zh`, `en`, `de`, in one table. REST (3): `GET /meta/:type/:name` and `GET /meta/:type` under `zh-CN` and `en` through `RestServer` with `i18nServiceProvider` as the 14th constructor argument (position verified against rest-server.ts). Not pinned: edges (a)-(c) above and the authored-translation layer — all pre-existing paths. The diff's 3 deletions are comment lines (kanban 2, docblock 1): no existing assertion changed. The ablation (anchor line deleted → 5/12 spec, 1/7 objectql, 2/3 rest red; restored green) is the dev's reading on `ac138e64e`, read, not re-run.

**7. Gates — green on the head.** Check-runs on `c8e5fee888af…` were read four times: at 2026-10-28T10:44Z (44 runs, 23 `in_progress`), 2026-10-28T10:55Z (65 runs, 23 `in_progress`), then every two minutes until 2026-10-28T11:03Z: 67 runs, 57 `success`, 10 `skipped` (opt-in, matrix-stub and schedule-gate rows), 0 `failure`, 0 `in_progress`. The eight required contexts are each `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (8/8 shards), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI`; `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` and `Test UI` (16/16) too. The dev's 85/85 derived gates with exit 0 on `c8e5fee88` and the suites and ablation on `ac138e64e` are read as reported, not re-run (`Local-runs: none`). Head unchanged at every read.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` `patch`: a served-document behaviour fix with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` — kind `none` takes `patch`. `@object-ui/plugin-kanban` `patch`: a source comment, and a published package whose `src/**` the diff moves. One changeset, both lines, both declarations present. Correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

**F1 — the dev's open question (ADR-0029 D9.2a): answered — A, a declared deviation, right for this card.** D9.2a binds the three scalars and says in its own first paragraph that for `fields`, `validations` and `indexes` the fold "still does" run as before: `validations` is named as outside the clause, so A contradicts no ADR. What A deviates from is this translator's own convention (`translateObject` docblock: field `description` "follows the rule above, as every string this translator added since does" — `description`, `inlineTitle` and the embedded `listViews` are each judged by `valueOverridesPackagedBase`). The deviation is right because the comparison is a property of the PAIR of readers, not of one: `authoredRuleMessage` has no packaged base and applies the catalog unconditionally, so B would serve the tenant's rewrite on `/meta` and the packaged translation in the refusal — the card's split re-opened for exactly the rewritten rules — and field `label`, the card's named precedent, is already flat `catalog ?? document` here. The deviation is declared where it lives (the helper's docblock "No packaged-base comparison") and in the acceptance notes. What it leaves, stated plainly: under a non-default locale, a tenant who rewrote a rule's message in a D9 overlay (same rule name) now sees the packaged translation on `/meta` as well as in the refusal, where before this PR `/meta` showed the rewrite. The #8284 sentence "an explicit override beats a packaged default" holds on neither surface for rule messages; the refusal half pre-exists. The complete answer is D9.2a on BOTH readers — the validator comparing against the packaged owner's rule (the registry already holds `getPackagedObjectBase`), then this overlay following the convention — a validator-side card outside this claim's surface. The lane seat files it as a card (the #8284 class, on a surface the 2026-08-13 ruling did not reach); the acceptance note meets Prime Directive 10's floor, so this is owed, not a condition of the verdict. Nit: the docblock declares the deviation without the ADR's id; one `ADR-0029 D9.2a` token there would make it greppable (Prime Directive 13).

**F2 — the default-locale edge (dev-declared): answered in ①2(a).** The #15711 contract, pre-existing and shared with every overlay; not this PR's to move.

**F3 — a `ui/` path in a `domain:spec` PR: within the amended claim.** Comment 6466175269 widened the surface to the one comment and the changeset line; the file list matches it exactly. No governed path (`skills/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `.github/workflows/**`) is in the file list; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success.

**F4 — branch `claude/project-thread-h0y6db`, not `claude/issue-27135-*`: declared in the claim** (platform-assigned thread branch, written as measured); the `Claim:` comment decides ownership and the PR-body guards passed. Not a flag.

**F5 — not re-measured here:** the dev's reading that Studio's rule editors run on the draft or the `/layers` baseline, so a translated message cannot be saved back. I did not re-measure it; the class is the ADR-0029 D9.2a "honest edge" already recorded for every translated string the served body carries, unchanged in class by this PR.

## 维护者速读 (席位终稿)

- 改了什么：`translateObject` 现在也翻译校验规则的提示语 `validations[].message`。它读翻译包里 `objects.<对象>._validations.<规则>.message`，和服务器拒绝写入时用的是同一个键（`objectValidationMessageKey`）。所以 `/meta` 和服务器的拒绝提示，在同一语言下显示同一句话。看板关闭列的提示（#27133）随之显示译文，那段过时的代码注释也一并改正。
- 为什么改：中文、日文等部署里，同一条规则的说明，服务器提示是译文，看板上却是原文，用户会读到两种语言的两句话。
- 风险与回滚：没有 schema 变化，只是读取时多一层翻译覆盖。没有译文的规则保持原文。`fields`、`actions` 的翻译不变，缓存按语言区分也不变。回滚 = revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts` 里新增的 `translateObjectValidations`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest exec vitest run meta-object-validation-message-i18n` 预期全绿（同一规则、同一语言下，`/meta` 与拒绝提示一致）。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

席位意见：接受。契约复核 PASS（6467333940），确认只有一个键、`/meta` 与拒绝提示在各种情况下一致、其它翻译不受影响。开发提出的问题（校验提示不做“已打包原文”比较）复核判定为有声明的偏离，而且是对的：只改一边会重新造成两句话不一致。租户改写过的规则提示会被打包译文盖住，这是本 PR 之前就有的问题，另立卡 #27221，两边一起修。

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · `domain:spec` seat 3 · `os-support-ai` · session `session_01WGufzgbJhFoXYsLSe5WSPP` · 2026-10-28T11:07Z

Head: `c8e5fee888af2f7cad5ed0b42cc4813784e0027e` · card #27135 · claim 6465192030, amendment (the kanban comment) · triage 6463784251 (one key)

1. **形态:** a draft PR to `main`, `Fixes #27135`. 6 paths, +535 / −3:
   - `i18n-resolver.ts` and its test;
   - an objectql and a rest test;

   - one changeset.

   All are inside the amended claim surface. `check-governed-merges --pr 27202` reports NOT governed (538 lines), so the ordinary queue landing applies. The assignee is `os-support-ai`.
2. **前提实测:** the premise holds on main. `translateObject` overlays `fields` and `actions` but not `validations[].message`, while the rule validator translates the refusal through `objectValidationMessageKey`. The review read the head and confirmed four things:
   - `translateObjectValidations` reads that key verbatim, through the shared locale ladder.
   - `/meta` equals the refusal for a nameless rule, a missing entry, inactive / warning-only rules, an extended object, the tenant authored layer and conditional branches. Three edges can differ (#15711 default-locale skip, an empty-string entry, the memory-i18n default leg); all are pre-existing and shared with field labels.
   - The `fields` / `actions` / `listViews` overlays are untouched.
   - The ETag stays locale-keyed, with `Vary: Accept-Language`.
3. **门禁 check-runs (on this head):** 67 runs, 57 success, 10 skipped, none red or pending, read at 2026-10-28T11:03Z. All eight required contexts are green. Dev-side readings:
   - resolver suites and the ablation on `ac138e64e`;
   - dispatch gates on `c8e5fee88`: 85 derived, 85 exit 0, 0 NOT-MEASURED.

   `c8e5fee88` adds only the kanban comment and its changeset line.
4. **接受的偏差:** (a) Validation messages use a flat `catalog ?? document`, with no ADR-0029 D9.2a packaged-base comparison. This is declared in the helper docblock and in Acceptance notes, and the review judged it right for this card: D9.2a names `validations` as outside its clause, and comparing on one reader alone would re-open the split. (b) The branch name is the platform-assigned thread branch.
5. **范围外去向:** a tenant-rewritten rule message loses to the packaged translation under a non-default locale. That is pre-existing on the refusal and now consistent on `/meta`; it is filed as #27221 (D9.2a on both readers). The public form door (`form-routes.ts` ~L317) now serves the translated message too, in the same direction as its refusal; that is named in the body. The review's nit (cite `ADR-0029 D9.2a` in the helper docblock) is not owed for landing.
6. **落地条款:** the seat checked the prose faces against the diff on this head: the PR body (with the second door and #27221 added in this round), the changeset, and the kanban comment. The seat readies the PR and arms auto-merge in this act, then follows it to MERGED.
